question.prompt: For a sequence \(u_1,\) \(u_2,\) \(\ldots,\) define \(\Delta^1(u_n)=u_{n+1}-u_n\) and, for all integers \(k\gt1,\) \(\Delta^k(u_n)=\Delta^1(\Delta^{k-1}(u_n)).\) If \(u_n=n^3+n,\) then \(\Delta^k(u_n)=0\) for all \(n\)

solutions.explanation:
Each application subtracts a formula at \(n\) from the same formula at \(n+1\). Keeping \(n\) symbolic lets us establish the result for every term, rather than just checking a few values.

First,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta^1(u_n)
&=(n+1)^3+(n+1)-(n^3+n)\\
&=3n^2+3n+2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Apply the same rule to this new sequence:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta^2(u_n)
&=3(n+1)^2+3(n+1)+2\\
&\quad -(3n^2+3n+2)\\
&=6n+6.
\end{aligned}
\]
The next two differences are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta^3(u_n)&=[6(n+1)+6]-(6n+6)=6,\\
\Delta^4(u_n)&=6-6=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
For positive integer indices \(n\), the first three differences are nonzero. The fourth is zero for every \(n\), and every higher difference remains zero because subtracting consecutive zeros again gives zero. Thus the answer is \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Apply the difference rule repeatedly
Expand the shift and subtract at every order
